Matchup-Driven

The backfield runs through one man — their top back absorbs 80% of the carries (league ~59%), a true bell-cow share that makes his rushing volume among the safest floors in the sport when the script cooperates.

The Offensive Blueprint

The WR2 is unusually involved here — 20% of targets (league ~15%), meaning there's bankable volume beyond the top receiver.

They live in the shotgun (80% of snaps vs ~68%) — a spread, pass-oriented structure.

They push it downfield — average depth of target 9.3 yards with 24% of throws traveling 15+, a vertical passing game that trades completions for boom-or-bust yardage.

They run downhill — mostly inside the tackles (20% to the edge vs ~25%), a gap/power scheme that trades big plays for a steady, grinding floor.

In the Red Zone

Inside the 20 they lean run-heavy, passing 44% of the time, funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back.

Defense — A Balanced Defense

Soft against opposing WR1s — 68 rec yds/game (vs ~58). A rec-yards target.

Soft against opposing tight ends — 42 rec yds/game (vs ~35). A rec-yards target.

They surrender 118 rushing and 253 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). No dominant funnel — read it matchup by matchup.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: no single dominant angle — this one's a matchup-by-matchup read.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
